To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(1) simply aggregating node embeddings does not lead effective link representations, (2) learning from labeled subgraphs around links provides effective link representations.

GNNs for learning link representations are more effective than GNNs for aggregating node representations, and that the subgraph-based methods outperform the aggregation-based methods in link prediction.

(1) GAE methods are less effective than SEAL for link prediction; (2) SEAL can achieve new state-of-the-arts on 3 out-of-4 datasets; and (3) we provide a thorough analysis to explain the success of SEAL.
